newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana passes marriage law to protect family.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana passes marriage law to protect family.

text.p: A pioneering state marriage law that would let couples choose to make it harder to divorce is designed to protect "the cornerstone of our society," the family, its drafter said on Tuesday.

The Louisiana legislature's passage late on Monday of a "covenant marriage" law marked a first victory for conservative Christians who have been campaigning to rewrite or overturn states' no-fault divorce laws, which they say undermine family stability.

"The whole intent is to try to strengthen the marriage," state Representative Tony Perkins said. The 34-year-old father of two drafted the bill that won approval in the final hours of the legislative session.
"The family unit is really the cornerstone of our society," he said, adding that despite revisions to his draft, "the concept is pretty much what we wanted."
Under the act, which Gov. Mike Foster is expected to sign into law shortly, couples could spurn a traditional marriage, to which no-fault divorce would still apply, for a covenant marriage.
They would then sign an agreement to undergo premarital counselling. If problems arose later, they would have to seek marital counselling before a legal separation could be granted.

Covenant marriages could be disolved only for adultery, a spouse's conviction on a felony charge that brought the death penalty or a sentence of hard labour, physical or sexual abuse, or abandonment. The only exception would be a two-year separation without reconciliation.
Current Louisiana law allows an immediate divorce if one spouse commits adultery or is sentenced to prison for a felony or if the couple has lived separately for six months.
Perkins said a 25-year study of the effects of divorce found it devastating to children, leaving them more disposed to violence and teen pregnancies.
